title: Relative Smooth Triangulation And Bundle Fitting

items.title: Relative smooth triangulations, strong approximation and bundle fitting
items.statement: A finite geometric simplicial complex $K$ is considered with its Euclidean realization and induced metric; subcomplex, closure, star and link terminology follows [[def-simplicial-subcomplex-star-closure-and-link]]. For $b\in|K|$ the **tangent star** is the union of the tangent cones at $b$ of all simplices containing $b$, that is, the rays locally contained in the closed star. A map $f:|K|\to M$ is **piecewise smooth** when every restriction $f|\sigma$ to a closed simplex extends smoothly to a neighbourhood in its affine hull and the extensions agree on common faces; in a target coordinate chart the differential $df_b$ is then the well-defined continuous piecewise linear map on the tangent star that equals $D(f|\sigma)(b)$ on the cone of each simplex $\sigma$ containing $b$. A **smooth immersion of a complex** requires $df_b$ injective on the entire tangent star at every point, not merely on each simplex tangent space; a **smooth embedding** requires in addition that $f$ be a homeomorphism onto its image, and a **finite smooth triangulation** of $M$ is such an embedding onto $M$. A corner-adapted triangulation must be face compatible: every local corner face is the image of a subcomplex, and the differential fan maps the source tangent star homeomorphically onto the appropriate tangent orthant, or its specified face sector. After an ambient Euclidean realization of the target, or in a fixed finite family of compact target chart patches, $g:K'\to M$ on a finite subdivision $K'$ of $K$ is a **strong $C^1$ $\delta$-approximation** to $f$ if $\sup_b|g(b)-f(b)|<\delta$ and $|dg_b(v)-df_b(v)|<\delta|v|$ for all $b$ and all tangent-star vectors $v$. A relative approximation **fixed on $L$** means $g|_{|L|}=f|_{|L|}$, subdivision of $L$ permitted unless explicitly prohibited. **Shape control** means a positive lower bound on $r(\sigma)/\operatorname{diam}\sigma$ for every positive-dimensional simplex, where $r(\sigma)$ is the distance from the barycentre to the relative boundary; it is not asserted for arbitrary iterated barycentric subdivisions. Two embeddings $f_i:K_i\to M$ **fit in a subcomplex** if the inverse images of $f_1(|K_1|)\cap f_2(|K_2|)$ are subcomplexes $L_i$ and $f_2^{-1}f_1:L_1\to L_2$ is a simplexwise affine isomorphism; the fit is **full** if every simplex all of whose vertices belong to $L_i$ belongs to $L_i$. Gluing along that isomorphism defines the union realization and union map. For a smooth bundle $\pi:E\to B$ and a supplied base triangulation $h:D\to B$, a **projection-preserving diagram** consists of $F:K\to E$ and a map $r:K\to D$ that is affine on each simplex into a simplex of the original $D$ and satisfies $\pi F=hr$; the affine/PL requirement does not require domain vertices to map to vertices of the original fixed base complex. Fitting preserves the projection when all modified maps satisfy the same equality with the original $h$ and the original affine $r$ restricted to their subdivisions; a fixed relative bundle piece must already carry such a diagram. No generic smooth map is called a bundle merely because it is proper. For relative extension on a compact manifold with corners, supplied boundary data are admissible only when they are compatible on all corner-face intersections and satisfy the tangent-orthant condition above; the extension keeps their pointwise parametrization, with compatible subdivisions permitted, and no extension of arbitrary incompatible boundary data is asserted.
items.strategy: This is a definition; the mathematical content is the contract itself, and no existence assertion is made here. Consistency facts that the later proofs use and that are fixed by the wording: agreement on common faces makes $df_b$ independent of the chosen containing simplex and continuous on the tangent star; gluing along a simplexwise affine isomorphism on a full subcomplex produces a well-defined finite complex and a well-defined union map; a projection-preserving diagram is determined by the pair $(F,r)$ together with its restrictions to subdivisions, so a modification supported away from a piece leaves the original diagram there exactly on the nose. The tangent-star formulation is deliberate: simplexwise injectivity of the differential is insufficient for an immersion, while injectivity on the whole tangent star is the condition stable under strong approximation (see the stability lemma below). No choice is used, and no mesh or shape bound is imposed on subdivisions unless a statement says so. The conventions for ``linear'' maps of complexes and for fitting in a (full) subcomplex are those of the cited sources, with domain vertices not required to map to vertices of a fixed base complex.
items.axiom_use: None: a definitional contract, using only the Euclidean realization and the induced metric.

items.title: Whole-star smooth embeddings are stable under strong piecewise C1 approximation
items.statement: Let $K$ be finite and $f:K\to\mathbb R^q$ a whole-star smooth immersion in the sense of [[def-relative-smooth-triangulation-and-projection-preserving-fitting]]. There is $\delta>0$ such that every strong piecewise $C^1$ $\delta$-approximation $g:K'\to\mathbb R^q$, on any finite subdivision $K'$, is a whole-star immersion. If $f$ is also an embedding, $\delta$ may be chosen so that $g$ is an embedding. The subdivision need not have a mesh or shape bound.
items.strategy:
Whole-star injectivity includes the affine tangent space of every simplex containing a point, so each simplex differential has full rank; on the unit sphere of each such tangent space $|D(f|\sigma)(b)v|$ has a positive minimum over the closed simplex, and the finite minimum over positive-dimensional simplices gives $\mu>0$ ([[thm-extreme-value-metric]]). Derivative norms changing by less than $\mu/2$ preserve ranks, and $|W-V|<\delta$ with $|V|\ge\mu$ forces the angle between $V$ and $W$ to be small, since $|W/|W|-V/|V||\le 2\delta/(\mu-\delta)$; thus strong derivative approximation gives arbitrarily small uniform angle approximation, independently of the subdivision.

For a proper common face $\tau=\sigma_1\cap\sigma_2$, project $p=(1-t)x+ty\in\sigma_1\setminus\tau$ (with $x\in\tau$, $y$ in the opposite face, $t\in(0,1]$) to $x_p=p+t(c-y)$, where $c$ is the barycentre of $\tau$; set $x_p=c$ for $t=1$. This projection is continuous, fixes $\tau$ and gives $p-x_p=t(y-c)$. Applied to the images under the linear embedding $df_b$ of the two simplices, the angle between $p-x_p$ and $z-x_p$ for $z\in\sigma_2$, $z\ne x_p$, is bounded below by the angle from $\sigma_1$ to $\sigma_2$: translate the ray $x_pz$ to start at $c$, extend it to the boundary of the truncated cone $\sigma_2-c$, and note that the endpoint ranges over a compact set on which its angle with $y-c$ has a positive minimum (equal ray directions would put a ray in both simplices outside their common face). Continuous dependence on $b$ makes the minimum over $b\in\tau$ positive; the finite minimum $\alpha>0$ over ordered pairs of simplices is therefore positive (take $\alpha=\pi/2$ when there are no such pairs).

Fix $b\in|K|$. Continuity of the finitely many simplex derivatives makes $f$ an angle approximation to the frozen piecewise linear map $df_b$ with tolerance $\alpha/8$ near $b$, and a sufficiently small $\delta$ makes $g$ an angle approximation to $f$, hence to that frozen map, with tolerance $\alpha/4$ on a common neighbourhood $U_b$. Shrink to a neighbourhood $V_b$ such that for $p,q\in V_b$ the two-segment path $pxq$ (midpoint when $p,q$ lie in one original simplex, the projection above otherwise) stays in $U_b$. Integrate each subdivided segment with [[cor-vector-valued-ftc-and-lipschitz-bound]]: the endpoint difference lies in the closed cone of vectors making angle at most $\alpha/4$ with its frozen image direction, whereas the two frozen rays from $x$ make angle at least $\alpha$ (or $\pi$ in the midpoint case), so the perturbed differences make angle at least $\alpha/2$ and cannot be equal. Hence $g(p)\ne g(q)$ for distinct $p,q\in V_b$, for every subdivision.

The same two-segment argument applied to the piecewise linear map $dg_b$, whose derivatives on each refined cone differ from $df_b$ by at most $\delta$, shows that $dg_b$ is injective on the tangent star: distinct cone vectors can be scaled simultaneously into the region where the projected paths are defined, and the positive rank bounds cover two vectors in one cone. Finitely many $V_b$ cover $|K|$, so all tolerances and the resulting $\delta$ can be chosen simultaneously, proving stability of immersion. If $f$ is an embedding, keep the cover and let $\eta>0$ be the minimum of $|f(p)-f(q)|$ over the compact set of pairs lying in no common $V_b$ (omit the constraint when that set is empty); with $\delta<\eta/3$ we get $|g(p)-g(q)|\ge\eta-2\delta>0$ on that set, while the $V_b$ separate all other distinct pairs. Then $g$ is continuous and injective on a compact space, hence a homeomorphism onto its image in the Hausdorff target, and together with the immersion statement it is an embedding. No mesh or shape bound on $K'$ is used.
items.axiom_use: None: finite minima over compact sets and segment integration.

items.title: Shape-controlled secants and relative piecewise smooth extension
items.statement:
Let $K$ be a finite geometric complex and $f:K\to\mathbb R^q$ piecewise smooth in the sense of [[def-relative-smooth-triangulation-and-projection-preserving-fitting]]. There are subdivisions $K_m$ agreeing on every original face, with mesh tending to zero and a single lower thickness bound $\theta>0$ for every positive-dimensional simplex, whose secant maps $S_m$, defined by affine interpolation of the values of $f$ at vertices, converge strongly in piecewise $C^1$ to $f$.

If $L\subset K$ is a subcomplex and $U$ an open neighbourhood of $|L|$, the approximation can instead be chosen pointwise equal to $f$ on a neighbourhood of $|L|$ and equal to a secant map outside $U$, on shape-controlled subdivisions; subdivision of $L$ is permitted and does not alter $f$ there, and every affine target-plane constraint already satisfied by $f$ on original simplices is preserved.

There is also a local extension statement: given a finite subcomplex $A\subset K$, a sufficiently small strong approximation $g$ to $f|_A$ on any subdivision extends to a prescribed small strong approximation $G$ to $f$ on a subdivision of $K$, with $G=f$ and with the original simplices unchanged outside the closed star of $A$. The permitted error of $g$ depends on the requested error and the finite original simplices, not on the shape of the subdivision of $A$. If the correction $g-f$ has zero component under an affine linear target map $p$ on $A$, then the extended correction has zero $p$ component everywhere. This last extension does not assert a shape bound on its coned simplices.
items.strategy:
Thickness construction. Realize the abstract complex as a union of faces of one standard simplex $\Delta\subset\mathbb R^N$ with vertices $0,e_1,\dots,e_N$; the original geometric realization differs by linear isomorphisms on finitely many simplices with uniformly bounded operator norms and inverse norms. In $\mathbb R^N$ cut the unit lattice cubes by the hyperplanes $\sum_i x_i=j$ and all their faces; the resulting locally finite convex cell complex has only finitely many cell shapes up to translation, so triangulating each cell compatibly ([[lem-finite-convex-cell-complexes-admit-compatible-triangulations]]) with a translation-invariant choice of interior point (for example the average of the vertices) gives finitely many simplex shapes, with maximal diameter $D$ and positive minimum thickness $\theta_0$ in positive dimensions. The simplex $m\Delta$, defined by $x_i\ge0$, $\sum_i x_i\le m$, and each of its faces are unions of these cells, so scaling by $1/m$ gives subdivisions of $\Delta$, and hence of $K$, with mesh at most $D/m$ and thickness at least $\theta_0$; restrictions to all faces agree because one global cell complex is used. Transport back to the original realization; the finitely many original simplices multiply diameter and inradius by factors bounded above and below, leaving one positive $\theta$. This is the lattice construction of Munkres 9.4; iterated barycentric subdivision does not have this property (9.4(a)).

Secant estimate. Let $s$ be a refined simplex inside an original simplex $\sigma$, with barycentre $b$, diameter $h$ and radius $r\ge\theta h$; put $T_b(x)=f(b)+Df(b)(x-b)$. On the compact $\sigma$ the derivative has a modulus of continuity $\omega_\sigma(h)\to0$, so segment integration ([[cor-vector-valued-ftc-and-lipschitz-bound]]) gives $|f(x)-T_b(x)|\le h\omega_\sigma(h)$ for $x\in s$. The affine difference $S_m-T_b$ interpolates the vertex errors, so its sup norm is at most $h\omega_\sigma(h)$; for an affine map $A$ on $s$ with $\sup_s|A|\le E$, a unit vector $v$ in the affine span satisfies $|DA(v)|=|A(b+rv)-A(b)|/r\le2E/r$, whence $\|DS_m-Df(b)\|\le2\omega_\sigma(h)/\theta$ and, by the chain rule ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]) and derivative continuity, $\|DS_m-Df(x)\|\le(2/\theta+1)\omega_\sigma(h)$. Taking the maximum of the finitely many moduli over original simplices proves strong $C^1$ convergence, including vectors in every refined tangent cone.

Relative version. Subdivide barycentrically once if necessary so that $L$ is full ([[def-barycentric-subdivision-of-an-abstract-simplicial-complex]]: the vertices are face chains, and a chain all of whose barycentric vertices lie in $L$ lies in $L$). Then the sum $d$ of the barycentric coordinates at vertices outside $L$ is a global continuous piecewise affine nonnegative function with zero set exactly $|L|$, whose minimum on the compact complement of $U$ is positive. Choose a smooth scalar cutoff $\chi(d)$ that is $0$ near $d=0$ and $1$ on that complement; its piecewise derivative is bounded by a fixed constant. Set $g_m=f+\chi(d)(S_m-f)$: this fixes $f$ near $L$, is a secant map outside $U$, and its derivative error is bounded by that of $S_m$ plus the fixed cutoff-derivative constant times the value error, which tends to zero. Affine target planes are preserved, since both vertex interpolation and affine combinations of points in a plane stay in that plane.

Local extension. Extend a subdivision of $A$ combinatorially in increasing dimension: keep every original simplex outside its closed star, and for each affected simplex whose boundary has already been subdivided, cone that boundary subdivision from the original barycentre. These cones are simplices and agree on faces by the ray description of a simplex. For an original simplex $\sigma$ with barycentre $c$, write each $x\ne c$ uniquely as $x=c+t(y-c)$ with $0<t\le1$ and $y\in\partial\sigma$, choose a smooth scalar taper $a$ that is $0$ for $t\le1/3$ and $1$ for $t\ge2/3$, and define $G(x)=f(x)+a(t)e(y)$, $G(c)=f(c)$, where $e=g-f$; on each coned simplex this extends smoothly across $c$ (it equals $f$ near $c$) and takes the given boundary values. On $t\ge1/3$, $t$ is affine in $x$ divided by the fixed barycentre-to-face height and $y=c+(x-c)/t$, so $|Dt|$ and $\|Dy\|$ are bounded by constants depending only on the original simplex, not on the subdivision of $A$; therefore the value and derivative norms of the correction are bounded by $C_\sigma\|e\|_{C^1}$. Applying the construction to the finitely many affected simplices in increasing dimension, the product of these finite bounds converts any requested final error into a sufficient bound on the initial error, uniformly over all subdivisions of $A$. If $p$ is affine linear with $p(e)=0$ then $p(a(t)e(y))=0$, so a zero $p$ component is preserved; and $G=f$ outside the closed star of $A$ by construction. No shape bound is claimed for the coned simplices.

items.title: Corner-adapted strong approximations preserve orthant sides
items.statement:
Let $F:K\to[0,\infty)^c\times\mathbb R^{n-c}$ be a finite whole-star smooth embedding, and write $\rho_iF$ for its first $c$ coordinate functions. Assume for each original simplex $\sigma$ and each $i$ that $Z_{i,\sigma}=\{x\in\sigma:\rho_iF(x)=0\}$ is a union of faces and that, at every $b\in Z_{i,\sigma}$, the linear form $d(\rho_iF)_b$ on the tangent cone of $\sigma$ is nonnegative with zero set precisely the tangent cone of $Z_{i,\sigma}$. These are the adapted face/tangent conditions, not merely simplex rank conditions.

There is $\delta>0$ such that every strong $\delta$-approximation $G$ preserving each of these coordinate planes on the specified zero subcomplexes maps all of $K$ into the same closed orthant and has exactly the same coordinate zero sets. It is an embedding for this choice of $\delta$. Thus plane-preserving fitting and extension can be used in corner charts when the initial pieces satisfy these adapted face conditions.
items.strategy:
Fix $i$ and an original simplex $\sigma$. On the zero set $Z_{i,\sigma}$ the form $d(\rho_iF)_b$ is nonnegative on the tangent cone of $\sigma$ and vanishes exactly on the tangent cone of $Z_{i,\sigma}$; the zero set of a nonnegative linear functional on a convex cone is a face of the cone, so locally at a point of a face of $Z_{i,\sigma}$ the zero cone is a single face and the form is strictly positive on every other generating direction. The finitely many normalized generating directions give a positive minimum there, and the finitely many zero faces give finitely many neighbourhoods with a uniform positive lower bound; away from these neighbourhoods the continuous positive ratio $\rho_iF/\operatorname{dist}(\cdot,Z_{i,\sigma})$ has a positive minimum by [[thm-extreme-value-metric]].

Consequently there is $a>0$ with $\rho_iF(x)\ge a\operatorname{dist}(x,Z_{i,\sigma})$ on $\sigma$ whenever the zero set is nonempty. Near a zero face, project barycentric coordinates to that face by deleting the coordinates outside it and renormalizing those inside; on a neighbourhood where the sum of the retained coordinates is at least $1/2$ the segment to the projection has length at most a fixed constant times the distance to the face, and its outward displacement is a nonnegative combination of the nonzero generating directions whose supporting-form value is bounded below by the previous paragraph; integrating along the segment, after shrinking so the derivative varies by less than half that bound, gives the displayed lower bound. Finitely many faces give one constant $a$.

Let $G$ be a strong $\delta$-approximation that preserves the coordinate planes on the specified zero subcomplexes. For $x\in\sigma$ choose a closest point $z\in Z_{i,\sigma}$ (compactness); since $\rho_iG(z)=\rho_iF(z)=0$, segment integration of the piecewise smooth difference gives $|\rho_iG(x)-\rho_iF(x)|\le\delta|x-z|=\delta\operatorname{dist}(x,Z_{i,\sigma})$ ([[cor-vector-valued-ftc-and-lipschitz-bound]] applied and added over the finitely many refined pieces). With $\delta<a/2$ it follows that $\rho_iG(x)\ge(a/2)\operatorname{dist}(x,Z_{i,\sigma})$, so $\rho_iG$ is positive off the zero set and the zero sets of all coordinates are exactly the prescribed ones. If $Z_{i,\sigma}$ is empty, $\rho_iF$ has a positive compact minimum and a value error less than half of it keeps $\rho_iG$ positive everywhere on $\sigma$. Taking the minimum of these finitely many positive bounds and imposing the embedding bound of [[lem-piecewise-smooth-embeddings-are-stable-under-fine-c-one-approximation]] gives one $\delta$ with all the asserted properties. The adapted face/tangent hypotheses are essential: by Munkres 9.8(e), affine-plane preservation alone does not preserve a half-space, so the distance-uniform lower bound is exactly the missing side control.
items.axiom_use: None: compactness minima, a supporting-functional face argument and segment integration.

references.title: James R. Munkres, Elementary Differential Topology, revised edition (1966); §9.8(d),(e) printed p. 96: affine-plane preservation for the tapered extension, and the explicit warning that plane preservation does not imply half-plane preservation; the local orthant-side argument is supplied here

items.title: Finite smooth fitting with exact bundle projection and protected regions
items.statement:
Let $F:K\to M$ and $G:L\to M$ be whole-star smooth embeddings of finite complexes into a smooth manifold without boundary. Given any positive strong $C^1$ tolerance, there are approximations on finite subdivisions fitting in a full subcomplex whose union is a whole-star smooth embedding.

The same conclusion holds for bundle diagrams $\pi F=hr_K$, $\pi G=hr_L$ over a fixed whole-star smooth base embedding $h:D\to B$, when all relevant images are in a smooth bundle with product trivializations. The final approximations satisfy these same diagrams with $h$ and $r_K,r_L$ unchanged as point maps, so the bundle projection is preserved exactly. The union map has the induced affine map to $D$.

The construction may be supported in a prescribed open neighbourhood $V$ of the new piece being fitted, including only the old pieces whose images meet that neighbourhood. In particular it fixes a closed protected region $R$ pointwise whenever all newly processed pieces and their required closed stars have images in $V$, with $\overline V\cap R=\varnothing$, and the maps already fit on the pieces outside this support. This is the fixed-collar relative interface: it does not assert arbitrary pointwise fixed-side fitting without the neighbourhood/separation hypotheses. Additional local affine plane constraints are preserved if the chosen charts make them coordinate planes and the already supplied diagrams respect them. For corner targets the same construction applies when all pieces satisfy the adapted face/tangent hypotheses of [[lem-corner-adapted-strong-approximations-remain-in-the-same-orthant]] in these charts; that lemma proves every altered piece remains in its original orthant.
items.strategy:
Euclidean fitting step. Two finite linear embedded complexes in $\mathbb R^q$ can be placed in one finite convex cell complex even when their underlying sets differ: cut a bounding box by all affine hyperplanes defining the affine hulls and barycentric facet inequalities of the finitely many simplices of both complexes. Each resulting cell is determined by choosing one weak side of each hyperplane; intersection activates further equalities and is a common face; each original simplex is a union of cells because its equalities and weak inequalities are among the cuts; and a cell is either contained in a given simplex or disjoint from it. Triangulate this complex compatibly ([[lem-finite-convex-cell-complexes-admit-compatible-triangulations]]) and restrict to the two original polyhedra; their intersection is now a subcomplex, and one barycentric subdivision makes it full (if a face chain has all barycentric vertices in the intersection, its largest face lies there, hence the whole simplex does). Pulling these subdivisions back through the linear embeddings gives fitting in a full subcomplex by arbitrary-overlap refinement; no same-polyhedron common-refinement theorem is used beyond its scope.

Local fitting of an attached piece. Work in $\mathbb R^q$ with a finite complex $P=Q\cup A$ and a piecewise smooth map $T$ such that $T|_Q$ and $T|_A$ are embeddings, $A$ being the new piece. Let $P_0$ contain the closed stars of all simplices meeting $T^{-1}(T(A))$ and let $P_1$ be its closed star; then $T^{-1}(T(A))$ lies in the relative interior of $|P_0|$, so the compact image of the complement of that interior has positive distance from $T(A)$. Choose the approximation tolerance below a quarter of that distance and small enough for [[lem-piecewise-smooth-embeddings-are-stable-under-fine-c-one-approximation]] on the two separate embeddings, and use [[lem-relative-shape-controlled-secants-approximate-smooth-simplex-maps]] to make $T$ secant on $P_1$ and to extend the change over its star while leaving $T$ outside. Every new intersection of the two images lies in $P_0$ by the distance bound and the triangle inequality, and both maps remain embeddings; on $P_1$ they are linear on a finite subdivision, where the Euclidean step fits them. Pull the subdivisions back and extend them over the whole complexes by coning subdivided faces from original simplex barycentres without changing the altered map. The union is a whole-star embedding: at a point of the intersection a neighbourhood is an actual geometric linear complex whose differential is the translated affine realization, hence injective on the whole tangent star; elsewhere one is locally inside a single embedded piece; the glued map is continuous and bijective from a compact space, hence a homeomorphism.

Bundle projection. In a product chart $M=B\times N$ write $T(x)=(h(r(x)),v(x))$. If $h$ is affine on every base simplex reached by the affected domain simplices, a secant of $T$ still has first coordinate $hr$ (both $r$ and $h$ are affine there and the secant matches vertex values), and every boundary correction has zero first coordinate, so the tapered extension preserves $\pi T=hr$ exactly; injectivity of $h$ forces equal $r$-values on identified points, so $r$ descends to the glued union and is affine on its simplices. In general, subdivide and choose a secant approximation $h'$ of $h$ on a finite base subcomplex covering the affected projections and their stars, extend it with the shape-controlled lemmas, and temporarily replace $T$ by $T_1=(h'r,v)$: equality of two $T_1$-values gives equal $r$, then equal $v$, hence equal $T$-values, and at the differential level injectivity of $h'$ and of the whole-star $dT$ gives injectivity on the tangent star, so $T_1$ is again an embedding. Apply the affine-base fitting to obtain $T_2=(h'r,v')$, then shift back to $T_3=(hr,v')$: the same argument shows each embedding and the embedding of their fitted union survive, and two points intersect under $T_3$ exactly when they intersect under $T_2$, because $h$ and $h'$ are injective and the fibre coordinate is unchanged. The first-coordinate changes cancel, leaving the original diagram; choosing the temporary secant and fitting errors successively small gives the prescribed final strong error by the chain rule ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]) on finitely many compact charts.

Finite induction and supports. In a general smooth target, subdivide the new complex so that each closed simplex and the old pieces in its intersection neighbourhood lie in one coordinate chart; in the bundle case choose product charts and base charts with the same property. Order the finitely many new simplices with faces first. Start with the old embedding and suppose the already processed new simplices fit it in a full subcomplex and their union is an embedding; attach the next simplex along its already processed boundary, giving $P=Q\cup A$, and apply the local step, or the projection-preserving steps in product charts. The changed map on the processed new subcomplex extends over the unprocessed simplices with arbitrarily small prescribed error, and in product charts its correction has zero base component, so the diagram is preserved. Choose the error at each of the finitely many stages small enough to retain the previous embeddings and fit margins, with total error below the requested tolerance. Unlike a locally finite argument, no unevidenced limiting map or infinite subdivision arises. Every local change and its extension is supported on the closed stars used in that construction, so if those supports have images in $V$ disjoint from the protected region $R$, the parametrizations and diagrams on $R$ are untouched and previously fitted pieces keep their identifications. Affine-plane constraints are preserved because secants and correction translations stay in the planes; for corner targets, after each plane-preserving local change the image still lies in the chart orthant by [[lem-corner-adapted-strong-approximations-remain-in-the-same-orthant]], before the chart inverse is applied.
items.axiom_use: None: finite fitting inductions on compact pieces, with the finitely many charts and simplices chosen explicitly.

items.title: Finite smooth triangulation of compact corners, relative to admissible boundary data
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice as an ambient hypothesis; the finite construction and the ODE interfaces below use no additional choice, so this hypothesis is dispensable. A smooth manifold with corners here is Hausdorff and second countable, with charts in relatively open subsets of $[0,\infty)^c\times\mathbb R^{n-c}$ and transition maps smoothly extendible with invertible derivative at corner points; transitions preserve the local depth and its face germs. Let $M$ be compact. Then $M$ has a finite corner-adapted whole-star smooth triangulation. Every local corner face, and any specified finite union of such closed faces, is a subpolyhedron.

If the total boundary already has a finite piecewise smooth triangulation $f:L\to\partial M$ compatible on all local face intersections, with its differential fan giving a homeomorphism onto the union of boundary faces of the tangent orthant at each point, the triangulation extends to $M$, pointwise preserving $f$ with compatible subdivisions allowed. In the resulting finite union construction all intersections may be made full subcomplexes. The same relative conclusion applies to a fixed triangulated closed neighbourhood piece whose smaller protected subcomplex lies in its relative interior: fitting is performed away from that protected subcomplex. No extension of arbitrary incompatible boundary data is asserted.
items.strategy:
Box pieces. If $M$ is empty take the empty complex; if $M$ has dimension zero, compactness makes it a finite discrete set. Otherwise choose finitely many corner charts and closed coordinate boxes $Q_i=[0,R_i]^{c_i}\times[-R_i,R_i]^{n-c_i}$ contained in them whose smaller relative interiors cover $M$; at a point of smaller depth shrink the chart so that all remaining corner coordinates are strictly positive and treated as ordinary. Each box has a finite cell triangulation ([[lem-finite-convex-cell-complexes-admit-compatible-triangulations]]), and its inverse chart map is a whole-star embedding, being the restriction of an invertible smooth coordinate map to an actual geometric complex; the preimages of the local corner planes are subcomplexes. In any other corner chart on an overlap the transition and its inverse map the corresponding tangent orthant and its faces isomorphically to the target orthant and faces (their derivatives preserve these tangent cones by taking directional limits), so the adapted face/tangent hypotheses of [[lem-corner-adapted-strong-approximations-remain-in-the-same-orthant]] hold for the box pieces in every chart used to fit them.

Collar. If the boundary is empty, the nonrelative construction also gives the relative result. For nonempty boundary, build a piecewise smooth collar directly. Around each boundary point choose a small corner chart and a smooth vector field whose active corner-coordinate components are strictly positive; restrict ordinary Euclidean smooth bump functions to these orthants, extend by zero, normalize their finite sum and form the weighted sum $V$, which is strictly inward along every active local face, because the inward tangent cone is preserved by chart transitions and its strict interior is convex. Extend $V$ over $M$ by the same finite bump construction; in each corner chart its coefficients extend smoothly to a neighbourhood in $\mathbb R^n$, so [[thm-picard-lindelof-local-existence-and-uniqueness]] solves the local ODE and uniqueness makes the solutions agree while in $M$; compactness gives a common positive time for starts on $\partial M$, and [[thm-smooth-dependence-of-ode-solutions-on-parameters]] gives smooth dependence on the initial point. The forward flow lies in the interior for small positive times because every active boundary coordinate has positive derivative. The map $\partial M\times[0,\epsilon]\to M$, $(y,t)\mapsto\Phi(y,t)$, is injective for small $\epsilon$: if two values agree, reverse the common interior orbit by uniqueness; different times would make an earlier boundary start occur at positive time on an orbit starting elsewhere, impossible once that orbit has entered the interior; equal times give equal starts. On the compact product it is a homeomorphism onto its image, which contains a neighbourhood of $\partial M$, since following $-V$ decreases a first active face coordinate at a uniformly positive rate until it reaches zero, within a time bounded by a constant times the distance to the boundary; finitely many boundary charts give a uniform neighbourhood and time. Composing with the supplied admissible boundary triangulation $f$ gives a corner collar: on each boundary simplex the product $L\times[0,\epsilon]$ is smooth, and at a corner the differential $(w,t)\mapsto df(w)+tV$ is injective on the full tangent star and fills the orthant, each orthant vector having the unique expression $v=w+tV$ with $t=\min_j v_j/V_j$ over the active corner coordinates.

Fitting and coverage. Fit the box pieces and the collar to one another using the supported construction of [[lem-relative-smooth-triangulations-can-be-fitted-while-preserving-a-bundle-projection]]; the additional verification in a corner chart is that the specified corner planes are affine, so the fitting keeps simplices in their planes, and [[lem-corner-adapted-strong-approximations-remain-in-the-same-orthant]] keeps every altered piece in its orthant with unchanged face zero sets; the support margins keep the images inside the relatively open charts. On overlaps the local face germs are permuted by the chart transition, so preserving them in the active chart preserves the same geometric faces in every chart. To see that the union covers $M$ rather than merely lying close to it: each initial box has a compact smaller core, and in its coordinates a sufficiently small perturbation of its map is $x\mapsto x+e(x)$ with $\|e\|_\infty$ less than the margin of that core from the artificial box faces and $e_j(x)=0$ on $x_j=0$ for a true corner face. For a target $y$ in the smaller core the self-map $x\mapsto\operatorname{clip}_{Q_i}(y-e(x))$ of the box (or of a ball under a radial parametrization) has a fixed point by [[thm-brouwer-fixed-point-theorem]]; clipping at an artificial face cannot occur at a fixed point because the error is smaller than the core margin; at a true corner face $x_j=0$ the constraint $e_j(x)=0$ makes clipped equality imply $y_j=0$ and the original equation $x_j+e_j(x)=y_j$ still holds; for unclipped coordinates it holds by definition. So the perturbed box still contains its entire core, and choosing the total fitting error below all finitely many margins makes the union image equal to $M$. The local differential fans are homeomorphisms onto the tangent orthants: for a target ray $y+tv$, preimages $x_t$ under the finite union homeomorphism converge to the preimage $b$ of $y$ and lie in one closed simplex containing $b$ on a subsequence; full rank gives $|x_t-b|\le Ct$, and a subsequential limit of $(x_t-b)/t$ is a tangent-cone vector mapping to $v$, while injectivity of the fan (the immersion statement) gives continuity of the resulting finite piecewise linear inverse. Thus the union is a finite corner-adapted whole-star smooth triangulation and all intersections are full after the prescribed barycentric refinement.

Relative case. Given the admissible boundary triangulation $f$, triangulate the finite product cells $\sigma\times[0,2\epsilon/3]$, $\sigma\in L$, keeping the given bottom-face subdivisions and coning the untriangulated higher cells; composing with the collar flow gives a whole-star embedding agreeing with $f$ on its bottom. Protect the smaller collar through time $\epsilon/4$. The compact complement of the open collar through time $\epsilon/3$ lies in the smooth interior of $M$ and is covered by finitely many ordinary closed chart boxes whose smaller cores cover it; choose them and all fitting stars disjoint from the protected collar. Fit these boxes and the outer collar pieces with the supported construction; all modifications occur away from the protected region in a boundaryless interior target, so the original $f$ remains pointwise fixed, while the coverage argument of the previous paragraph applies to the interior cores and to the compact intermediate collar annulus. A fixed triangulated closed neighbourhood piece with a smaller protected subcomplex is handled by the same supported fitting and core-coverage argument. The construction uses only finitely many chart pieces and finite subdivisions, keeps the face zero sets, and never inverts a corner chart outside its domain; no extension of arbitrary incompatible boundary data is asserted.
items.axiom_use: The Axiom of Choice is declared as an ambient hypothesis and carried in deps for the frozen manifest graph, but no essential use is identified: the finitely many charts, bumps and ODE data involve only finite choices, and the cited Picard-Lindelof and smooth-dependence suppliers are choice-free.

references.title: James R. Munkres, Elementary Differential Topology, revised edition (1966); §10.6 boundary-extension proof printed pp. 103-105, with Theorem 10.4 printed pp. 101-103 and Exercise 10.4(a),(b) printed p. 103; the corner side control and the total-boundary collar construction are additional arguments supplied here (Munkres 10.6 treats boundary, not corners)

items.title: Finite smooth bundle triangulation over a fixed base, relative to a supplied collar diagram
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\pi:E\to B$ be a smooth bundle with compact total space, compact smooth base and compact smooth fibre, permitting corners. A bundle here comes with finite smooth local product trivializations, whose transition maps preserve all local source/target corner faces; a boundary face in a product chart is either a base face or a fibre face. Let $h:D\to B$ be a supplied finite corner-adapted whole-star smooth triangulation.

Then there is a finite corner-adapted whole-star smooth triangulation $F:K\to E$ and a piecewise affine map $r:K\to D$ with $\pi F=hr$. Thus the actual bundle projection is PL over the fixed base parametrization. Refining base pieces for local construction does not change $h$ or the original complex $D$ in the final diagram: $r$ on a domain simplex is affine into a simplex of the original $D$.

The construction is relative to any supplied finite diagram $C:J\to E$, $\pi C=hr_J$, embedding onto a closed neighbourhood of a protected subpolyhedron $R$ contained in its relative interior, provided the fitting supports of the remaining pieces can be chosen disjoint from $R$. In particular this applies when $C$ is an already triangulated collar neighbourhood of the entire boundary and $R$ is a smaller collar: the original boundary and all its corner-face intersections are kept pointwise, with compatible subdivisions allowed. All union intersections are full subcomplexes.

This relative contract requires the collar diagram, not just an arbitrary triangulation of the boundary without any projection-preserving neighbourhood extension. Nor does proper smoothness of $\pi$ alone replace the supplied bundle trivializations.
items.strategy:
Fibre and base pieces. If $E$ is empty take the empty total complex and map. Otherwise triangulate the compact fibre $N$ by [[thm-compact-smooth-manifolds-with-corners-admit-relative-finite-triangulations]], say $g:L\to N$. Subdivide $D$ finely enough that the closed stars of the relevant simplices have images under $h$ in the base domains of the finitely many bundle product charts: continuity of $h$ and the finite product-chart cover give a positive Lebesgue margin on the compact realization, and the mesh can be made as small as needed. Choose finitely many closed base subcomplex pieces $D_i$ with interiors covering $D$ and $h(D_i)$ compactly contained in a product-chart base domain, the subdivision inclusion being affine on each simplex into an original simplex of $D$. For each $i$ the product map $F_i(x,y)=\phi_i(h(x),g(y))$ on $D_i\times L$ is a whole-star smooth embedding (the product of embeddings through a face-compatible product chart); triangulate its finite product cells compatibly ([[lem-finite-convex-cell-complexes-admit-compatible-triangulations]]), so that projection onto $D_i$ is affine on each product simplex and $\pi F_i=h\operatorname{pr}_1$. The face/tangent conditions transfer from those of $h$ and $g$ and the face-compatible product chart, so these are admissible bundle diagrams.

Fitting. Apply [[lem-relative-smooth-triangulations-can-be-fitted-while-preserving-a-bundle-projection]] to fit the finitely many diagrams in turn, choosing the accumulated strong error as small as needed on every compact chart. The fitting construction never changes $h$ or the original point map $r_i=\operatorname{pr}_1$ of a piece, and on an identified overlap injectivity of $h$ forces the same base point, so the maps $r_i$ descend to one map $r$ on the glued finite complex; after the subdivisions each is still affine into a simplex of the original $D$, so $r$ is a valid final affine-base map. The union map is a whole-star embedding, all intersections are full, and [[lem-corner-adapted-strong-approximations-remain-in-the-same-orthant]] retains every corner face.

Coverage fibre by fibre. Fix $x\in D_i$ and $b=h(x)$. Since the original $r_i$ is unchanged, the perturbed embedding $F_i'$ maps the entire slice $\{x\}\times|L|$ into the same fibre $E_b$, with original fibre map $g$. Cover $N$ by finitely many closed local corner boxes by their smaller cores and parametrize the input slice over one such box by $g^{-1}$ (continuous because $g$ is a homeomorphism); there the perturbed fibre map is a continuous small perturbation $u\mapsto u+e(u)$ of the identity, uniformly in $x$, with $e_j=0$ on every true fibre-boundary face because the fitting preserved those zero sets ([[lem-corner-adapted-strong-approximations-remain-in-the-same-orthant]]). For a target point $v$ in the smaller core the self-map $u\mapsto\operatorname{clip}(v-e(u))$ of the box has a fixed point by [[thm-brouwer-fixed-point-theorem]]; if the error is below the core margin no artificial box face can clip at a fixed point, and at a true face $u_j=0$ the constraint $e_j=0$ makes clipped equality imply $v_j=0$, so the original equation still holds and $v$ lies in the perturbed slice. Hence each perturbed slice hits every core and therefore all of $N$; since the $D_i$ cover the base, the union embedding is onto $E$ and is the required triangulation.

Relative case. Start with the supplied diagram $C:J\to E$, $\pi C=hr_J$, embedding onto a closed neighbourhood of the protected subpolyhedron $R$ in its relative interior. Cover the compact complement of a still smaller open neighbourhood contained in $C(J)$ by finitely many local product pieces of the form $D_i\times Q_i$, with $Q_i$ a closed fibre coordinate box; the separation hypothesis and compactness let us choose their images and all necessary fitting stars disjoint from $R$. The domain base pieces come from sufficiently fine subdivisions of $D$, and the product simplices retain affine projection into the original $D$. Fit these pieces to $C$ and to one another by the supported construction, which leaves $C$ pointwise unchanged on $R$ and keeps the exact original projection on every piece; the smaller cores still cover the complement by the box fixed-point argument, the compact intermediate overlap in the old neighbourhood piece is retained under a sufficiently small approximation, and the protected region itself is untouched. In the collar application the entire boundary lies in $R$, so the prescribed boundary parametrization and all its corner-face intersections remain fixed, with compatible subdivisions. All constructions are finite; no Ehresmann theorem, generic algebraic-map triangulation or unproved smooth fitting primitive is substituted for the actual product charts and the local fitting proof.
items.axiom_use: The Axiom of Choice is assumed in the Statement and declared in deps; the finite product-chart construction uses only finite choices, and the cited ODE, Brouwer and fitting suppliers are choice-free, so no essential AC use is identified beyond the ambient declaration retained by the frozen manifest graph.

references.title: H. Putz, Triangulation of fibre bundles, Canadian Journal of Mathematics 19 (1967); §2.1-2.5 diagram fitting and the bundle-triangulation corollaries over a fixed base (2.2), fibre with boundary (2.3-2.4) and compatible subbundle (2.5), printed pp. 501-505; §2.8-2.9 relative approximation and common subdivisions printed p. 506; §3.3-4.4 fitting and its finite induction printed pp. 509-512; the compact corner contract and the explicit protected-neighbourhood clause are additional arguments supplied here

items.title: Projection-preserving product triangulation of a trivial smooth bundle
items.statement: Let $h:D\to B$ and $g:L\to N$ be supplied finite corner-adapted whole-star smooth triangulations. The trivial bundle $\pi:B\times N\to B$ has a finite smooth triangulation $F:K\to B\times N$ satisfying $\pi F=hr$ for a piecewise affine map $r:K\to D$, with $h$ unchanged. Product corner faces are subpolyhedra.
items.strategy: The cells $\sigma\times\tau$ with $\sigma$ a simplex of $D$ and $\tau$ a simplex of $L$ form a finite convex cell complex: the intersection of two is the product of their respective common faces, hence a common face. Apply [[lem-finite-convex-cell-complexes-admit-compatible-triangulations]] to obtain a finite compatible triangulation $K$ of $|D|\times|L|$. Define $F(x,y)=(h(x),g(y))$ and $r(x,y)=x$: every simplex of $K$ lies in a product cell, so $F$ is smooth there with matching face values, $r$ is affine into a simplex of the original $D$, and $\pi F=hr$ holds pointwise with $h$ unchanged. The product map is a homeomorphism because both factors are, and its tangent-star differential $(u,v)\mapsto(dh(u),dg(v))$ is injective: equality of two images gives $dh(u)=dh(u')$ and $dg(v)=dg(v')$, and the whole-star hypotheses give $u=u'$, $v=v'$, even after the product-cell subdivision. The corner-face fans and their zero sets are products of those of the factors, so the triangulation is corner adapted, and every product face is a union of the triangulated cells. The construction is elementary and does not invoke the general bundle theorem.
items.axiom_use: None: an explicit finite product-cell triangulation.
